s2_cf1_root_cause_and_scope.root_cause: PLAN containment is deliberately non-terminal (P4B: a contained PLAN failure must stay retryable so a live service can re-plan on the next invocation). A ONE-SHOT driver ends its process right after the cycle, so the non-terminal row outlives the process with no terminalizer — recovery only runs at the NEXT service startup, which a one-shot context never reaches. The defect is the missing invocation-exit boundary owner, NOT the PLAN containment semantics themselves.
s2_cf1_root_cause_and_scope.impact_scope: every one-shot benchmark/diagnostic execution whose cycle ended without finalization (valid plan + gate denial, PLAN containment, provider timeout, cancellation) persisted 'running' indefinitely; equivalent contained-model-failure causes produced asymmetric durable records (INTEGRATE failures read failed, PLAN failures read running). Live-service behavior was never affected and remains unchanged.

s4_final_settlement_design: One-Shot CLI execution -> Agent execution returns or raises -> one-shot exit boundary (inside _async_run, before evaluation and artifact persistence) -> targeted AgentRun settlement over the execution's OWN task/investigation/run ids -> durable status verification (re-read; any remaining non-terminal run raises) -> benchmark artifact finalization (settlement.json written beside run_manifest/snapshot/result/failure). Cause mapping uses existing vocabulary only: cancelled execution -> cancel_run(cancelled); contained supervisor failure -> fail_run(internal_failure, error_code=<trajectory-recorded code verbatim>); finalization denied -> fail_run(budget_exhausted, error_code=finalization_denied); ended without finalization -> fail_run(budget_exhausted, error_code=one_shot_exit_without_finalization).
s5_why_fit_for_one_shot_without_touching: The settlement lives entirely in the benchmark driver's exit boundary: the live service never calls it, and the orchestrator/PLAN semantics it relies on are untouched. In a live service PLAN containment still leaves the run retryable and the next invocation re-plans into the SAME run — verified unchanged (the RCA-2A.2c lifecycle tests pin the orchestrator-level semantics and still pass). The adapter settles only runs under the execution's own investigation id, so even if a store held foreign runs they are not scanned or modified (T10). Recovery keeps its exclusive role: abnormal-interrupt cleanup. The two are never invoked for each other's job.
s6_sqlite_state_and_transaction_rules: Every settlement transition is one repository transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE): status transition validation against RUN_TRANSITIONS + trajectory append + commit, all-or-nothing. The adapter reads the persisted status first (friendly no-op), then attempts the transition; if a concurrent transition won the race the AgentRuntimeConflictError path re-reads and reports lost_race_no_regression — terminal states can never regress. A transition whose result does not durably terminalize the run raises ('did not persist') — a settlement that cannot persist NEVER reports success (T6), and the leftover row remains on the existing recovery path.
